brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: There are 5 hex-acc-keyhole accessories on one face: accessory:0#-1,0#2, 0#0,0#2, 0#1,0#2, 1#-1,0#2 and 1#1,0#2. The hooks are all on the opposite face. How much weight the hangers and wall screws can hold depends on the material and screws, which the configurator doesn't check.

12 hex-acc-hook plates, two hooks each (24 hooks), on slots 4 and 5 of all six cells, facing away from the wall. The preview only lets props hang on hooks as cable, tape or goggles, not as hand tools, so I showed a roll of gaffer tape and a coiled cable on the top hooks. A second gaffer tape roll was refused because it overlapped the cable. Hanging actual tools on the hooks isn't shown.

requirements.requirement: Rack holds together as one unit
requirements.evidence: Joint bolts lock each row's pieces together. check_build reports no rule errors and the mesh-collision check is clear. It lists 4 faces that could take a cap, which I left open.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack that's 3 cells wide and 2 storeys tall, from 6 full hex pieces. It has 5 keyhole hangers on one face (3 on the bottom row, 2 at the top corners) and 12 hook plates on the opposite face, with two hooks per plate, for 24 hooks in total. I ran end caps and joint bolts across it. check_build reports no rule errors and the mesh-collision check is clear. It still lists 4 faces that could take a cap; I left those open. I added the second storey because the hooks on the bottom row sit too close to the bench for anything to hang from them in the preview. That brings the build to 51 parts and about 2.27 kg of filament, more than the roughly 40-part guide. To make it smaller, drop the top row: you're left with 3 cells, 3 keyholes and 6 hook plates.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
